Morning everyone, quick update from my side. We are running three things in parallel this month, so I will be short. First, the training. We are training the store managers and we are almost done, thirty-one out of forty-one. Second, the systems. We are still working with two systems at the same time, because the new one is not ready, and honestly it is costing us about six hours a week. I am not happy about that. Third, the job titles. We are not moving there, we are waiting for the model from headquarters. So that is my only real blocker. One good thing before I stop: people are asking a lot more questions than before, and they are asking them in the meetings and not in the corridor. For me that is the best sign we have.

There is one question I ask in every first interview, and candidates almost never prepare it. What are you working on right now? It sounds like small talk. It is not. I ask it because I want to hear if you are close to the work or far from it. When somebody answers with the job description, I learn nothing. When somebody says I am training forty store managers this month and we are at thirty-one, I know exactly who I am talking to. Two small things. Use the continuous, because right now is not the same as always. And say one thing that is not going well. Candidates who tell me only good news sound like a presentation, not like a person. The one who says this part is blocked and here is what I am doing about it, that is the one I call back.
